relevance_note: A PRISMA systematic review of ALPS-like disorders that mentions TNFAIP3 patients only as counts and group summaries (Supplementary table 1: 105 reported, 16 filtered; Table 1 'TNFAIP3' column; 'No ALPS-like patient with a defect in the PRKCD, XIAP, IL2RA, IL2RB, TPP2, STAT1 GOF, IL12RB1, ADA2 and TNFAIP3 genes presented malignancy'), with no individual-level detail for any TNFAIP3 carrier.
method_note: Read the whole Markdown, including the converted supplement (DataSheet_1.docx). TNFAIP3 appears only in group-level text, the Table 1 summary columns (the TNFAIP3 column is duplicated by the converter's merged-cell repetition), Supplementary table 1 counts, and reference entries 62 and 85. The functional assays shown from the authors' own laboratories (Figures 4-7) concern SAP, XIAP, MAGT1, PIK3R1, LRBA, CTLA4, STAT3 GOF and STAT1 GOF patients and a CVID patient, not TNFAIP3. So no individual rows. n_patients_reported = 16 is the 'Filtered cases' (ALPS-like) count for TNFAIP3 in Supplementary table 1, whose clinical data feed Table 1; the same row gives 105 'Reported cases' from 25 publications, which could also be read as the number of TNFAIP3 patients counted. cohort_size_as_stated = 645 ALPS-like patients across 24 genes ('Considering the cohort of 645 ALPS-like patients'); the search itself counted 2245 unique patients. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients = true because every patient is taken from earlier publications; the paper does not map Supplementary table 2 references to genes, so prior_report_citation lists only the references the text attaches to TNFAIP3 patients (62, 85). The text also cites '(27, 61, 62)' for viral infections in TET2, TPP2 and TNFAIP3 patients, which does not separate genes. No contradictions found. Publications row built with a short Python script; spans checked verbatim by script.
